subject: Third-party subprocessors & telemetry: follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@marketplace.io>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Subprocessors & telemetry questions from today

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo earlier  very helpful context. A few follow-up items from our security and procurement teams around telemetry/third-party sharing so we can progress the legal review: 

1) Which telemetry vendors does Redwood share telemetry with by default (e.g., Datadog, Sentry, Segment)? Are any of these considered subprocessors that see customer data (even aggregated)?

2) For telemetry that contains request/response metadata, do you apply any PII filtering or pseudonymization before sending to third parties?

3) Data retention: what are default retention windows for logs/telemetry at the platform layer, and can customers override them for our account?

4) Data residency: if we pin to a US-only tenant, do telemetry exports ever cross regions for processing/analysis?

5) Marketplace integrations: when using the marketplace flow (e.g., Marketplace.io), is any customer identifiable data passed to the marketplace provider?

We can share a short RFI if that helps  attaching a preliminary list of asks. Would appreciate a quick summary and any existing subprocessors matrix you can provide.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Security Manager, Acme AI
Samantha@acme.ai

[Attachment: Acme_telemetry_RFI.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Subprocessors & telemetry questions from today

Hi Samantha  great to meet you today, and thanks for the detailed list. Quick high-level answers below, and I've attached our latest subprocessors matrix for reference. Dev and Rishi are looped in for the technical details.

1) Telemetry vendors: by default we send platform-level metrics/traces to Datadog for infra monitoring. We send error/exception traces to Sentry (configurable). We do not send request/response payloads to these services.

2) PII filtering: we have request/response redaction hooks in the runtime. By default, any user-submitted text is not sent to third-party telemetry. We only surface hashed/session identifiers and sampling-limited traces. If a customer enables advanced debug logs, those are controlled via the "Debug Log" flag (opt-in) and are subject to stricter retention and export controls.

3) Retention: default telemetry retention is 90 days for metrics and 30 days for request-level logs; customers on Dedicated/Private tiers can request custom retention windows. We can surface a tenant-level retention setting for Acme as part of the Dedicated contract.

4) Data residency: when you pin to our US tenant we ensure model inference and storage live in the US region. Some telemetry processing (aggregations) may run in our analytics pipeline which is also US-hosted for US tenants  we can commit to US-only processing for the Marketplace flow if required.

5) Marketplace: Marketplace.io receives only billing and subscription metadata (account id, usage totals) when customers purchase via the marketplace. No request/response content or PII is passed to marketplace providers in our standard flow.

Next steps:
- See attached: Redwood_subprocessors_matrix_v2.pdf (contains vendor list and data categories).
- Dev/PPE: Dev, can you confirm the pseudonymization approach and whether we can add a tenant-level toggle to block 3rd-party telemetry exports for Acme?
- Marissa: Will follow up with a short SOC2/docs pack and a HubSpot note linking the RFI.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

[Attachment: Redwood_subprocessors_matrix_v2.pdf]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T13:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Subprocessors & telemetry questions from today

Hi Samantha  quick technical note to supplement Marissa's summary: 

- Telemetry flow: our runtime emits three classes of telemetry: aggregate metrics (counts/latency), sampled traces (span metadata, no payload), and debug logs (opt-in). Span metadata contains trace ids, service names, durations, and non-identifying annotations.

- Pseudonymization & PII: we apply a hashing layer to session/user ids before exporting; any fields that match common PII patterns (email, SSN patterns) are redacted by our sanitizer. We do not currently perform NLP-based PII detection on all payloads, only on debug logs when the customer enables the advanced debug setting.

- Tenant-level controls: we can add a tenant flag (block_external_telemetry_exports = true) that prevents any telemetry data from leaving the tenant boundary to third parties. That would be a Dedicated/Enterprise feature and we can scope work to have it available prior to contract execution for Acme.

- Marketplace integrations: marketplace providers only receive non-content billing metadata. We have a customers/partner review checklist before enabling marketplace flows.

If you can share the specific telemetry fields your security team is worried about (the RFI helps), I can map them against our matrix and provide a statement we can include in the DPA/SoW.

Thanks,
Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
dev.patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Subprocessors & telemetry questions from today

Marissa / Dev  thanks for the clear write-up and for the matrix. This is exactly what the procurement and security teams needed. A couple quick asks before we move to legal: 

- Can you provide a short statement we can attach to the RFI that confirms that no request/response content or customer PII is sent to Datadog/Sentry/Marketplace.io under the default configuration?
- Please confirm the timeline and scope/cost for enabling the tenant-level block_external_telemetry_exports flag (we can treat as a gating item for Dedicated onboarding).

If those look good, I'll push to Legal and Procurement and schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive next week (Alex will coordinate the marketplace side).

Best,
Samantha
